title: Kandy to Ella by Train: Riding the Most Scenic Railway on Earth
author: Adventure Guide Team
excerpt: From misty emerald tea plantations to the famous Nine Arch Bridge—here is how to book tickets, pick the best side of the carriage, and explore Ella.
content:
The Magic of Sri Lanka's Hill Country Railway

Winding through rolling Ceylon tea estates, cloud forests, rushing waterfalls, and colonial viaducts, the 6-to-7-hour train journey from Kandy to Ella is a bucket-list experience for every traveller visiting Sri Lanka.

Which Class Should You Book?

  • First Class Observation / A/C: Comfortable plush seating with panoramic windows, though windows do not open for photography.
  • Second Class Reserved: The sweet spot! You get a guaranteed seat, ceiling fans, and open windows to feel the cool mountain breeze.
  • Third Class Reserved: Budget-friendly and great for mingling with friendly local families and tea-samosa vendors.
Sit on the right side of the train from Kandy to Nuwara Eliya (Nanu Oya), and move to the left side from Nanu Oya to Ella for the most dramatic valley views.

Top Adventures Once You Arrive in Ella

Spend at least three nights in Ella to hike Little Adam's Peak at sunrise, watch the blue train cross the colonial Nine Arch Bridge in Demodara, and cool off at Ravana Falls.
